messages:
maria-support: Hey team — ACME reported a sudden drop in embeddings vectors/sec ~60% after the midnight deploy. Tokens/sec looks fine, but customers see timeouts and 500s when calling /v1/embeddings. Anyone else seeing this on the dashboards?

kai-eng-runtime: Looking at infra metrics now. GPU util is at 98% on the vec-serving pool, queue_depth spiked. Tokens/sec (text-gen) unchanged. Suspect batching changes in the last rollout. deploy-bot: deploy "embed-batcher-v2" succeeded 2026-02-06T00:10:12Z.

glen-eng-ml: Customer log snippet they attached: `{\"error\":\"dimension_mismatch\",\"expected_dim\":1536,\"got_dim\":1024}` — that would cause fallback + reconcilation overhead if many clients suddenly sent older model dims, but should be a quick rejection, not GPU saturation. Do we have a mixed-model routing issue?

sasha-eng-sre: I see a lot of backpressure loops in the queue: `kvcache-miss -> full-batch -> enqueue -> retry` pattern. When requests are rejected for dim mismatch we still allocate KV cache slots briefly, causing eviction churn. That plus the new batcher aggregation could be magnifying GC/alloc pressure.

maria-support: Repro steps from ACME: 1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"input":"...","model":"open-embed-1536","dimension":1536}' POST /v1/embeddings -> slow / sometimes 500. 2) Some clients still call `open-embed-1024` variant which returns 1024 vectors; our routing should separate them but looks like they're hitting same GPU pool.

kai-eng-runtime: Quick check: `kubectl get pods -n vecs -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,IMG:.spec.containers[*].image` shows batcher v2 on the same nodepool as the 1536 model. Current batch_window_ms=40 (v1 was 20). I pushed a test change to reduce to 20 on one canary, let's monitor. ops-bot: scaling vecs-pool +2 nodes (scale policy override).

ops-bot: scaled vecs-pool from 18 -> 20 nodes at 2026-02-06T00:28:09Z per request by sasha-eng-sre.

glen-eng-ml: Two hypotheses: (A) batching window bump increased average batch size so long sequences/KV cache hotlines consume GPU mem and push other shards to swap; (B) routing mis-tagging causing 1024 and 1536 variants to collide into same worker and cause extra tensor conversions. Need to inspect request headers and routing keys.

sasha-eng-sre: Grabbed live tail of router logs: `WARN route-mapper: fallback_route_used model=open-embed-1536 target=open-embed-1024 reason=variant_fallback` — yep, fallback storm. Something in rollout changed compatibility checks; fallback triggers extra decoding/encoding steps.

maria-support: ACME says the drop started at 00:12 UTC exactly, matches deploy timestamp. They provided a sample request that failed. I forwarded to support case #C-78122.

kai-eng-runtime: For immediate mitigation: 1) revert batcher v2 config to batch_window_ms=20 globally OR 2) pin routing of open-embed-1536 to its dedicated nodepool (quick but needs LB change). Which is faster?

sasha-eng-sre: Revert config is low-risk. I can flip batch_window back to 20 across pool in ~5 minutes. Pinning requires LB rollout and may be slower. I'll revert first.

kai-eng-runtime: Also opened quick metric dashboard: https://graf.redwood/intern/dashboards/vecs/throughput?from=2026-02-06T00:00&to=2026-02-06T01:00 — watch tokens/sec vs vectors/sec panels.

deploy-bot: configmap "embed-batcher-config" updated by sasha-eng-sre at 2026-02-06T00:34:10Z (batch_window_ms: 40 -> 20).

glen-eng-ml: After revert: vectors/sec climbed ~45% within 90s, GPU util dropped to ~70%, queue_depth normalized. Still seeing a small number of mismatch errors — need to patch the routing check to ensure variant header is enforced earlier in the proxy to avoid wasteful work.

maria-support: Customer confirmed partial recovery after your change. They still see some 500s at a low rate. Are we tracking affected API keys to notify customers?

sasha-eng-sre: Pulling logs for the last hour to extract keys with >5 errors. `jq -r '.api_key' < router_errors.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head` — doing that now.

kai-eng-runtime: Action items: - glen: PR to enforce variant header in proxy (enforce model_variant header before routing) - sasha: monitor for 2 hours, rollback if spikes return - maria: notify ACME with ETA and root cause update - ops: keep vecs pool +2 until tomorrow morning or until metrics stable.

glen-eng-ml: I'll target the PR today: checkin in ~2 hours. Quick patch: return 400 for wrong-dim before enqueuing to batch. That should avoid KV allocations. Example pseudo-patch in proxy: ```if req.model_variant != worker.expected_variant: return 400, "variant_mismatch"```

maria-support: Thanks all. I'll update the case with the rollback note and the mitigation steps. ACME asked if this was a billing issue since their requests retried; we're checking for double-charges and will offset if needed.

sasha-eng-sre: Metrics look stable at +90m. Leaving the +2 nodes for 6h buffer. I'll post a follow-up summary after 2h. :thumbsup:

maria-support: Follow-up: ACME confirmed degradation resolved. Closing internal incident, leaving support case open until patch lands.

ops-bot: Incident channel updated (incident-id: INC-2026-0206-vecs-batcher) and retention set to 7d.
